Dashboards & charts

Source: vignettes/charts.Rmd
charts.Rmd

shadshiny does not draw charts. It gives you the shell around them — shad_value_box() and shad_chart_container() — and the palette inside them, so a ggplot2, plotly, or echarts4r figure matches the page instead of fighting it.

KPI cards 

library(shiny)
library(shadshiny)

shad_value_box(
  value           = "$48,120",
  label           = "Revenue",
  delta           = "+12.4%",
  delta_direction = "up",       # "auto", "up", "down", "neutral"
  icon            = "activity",
  caption         = "vs. last month"
)

delta_direction = "auto" reads the sign off the delta string: a leading - or − renders the down/destructive chip, anything else renders up. Set it explicitly whenever “up” isn’t the good direction — churn going up is not a win.

sparkline takes any tag. Reach for shad_sparkline() before a plotOutput(): it is inline SVG with no plotting stack and, more usefully, its marks are painted with the theme’s chart tokens, so a dark-mode toggle or a preset switch restyles it in CSS — no re-render, no server round-trip.

shad_value_box("1,204", "Sessions", delta = "-3.1%",
               sparkline = shad_sparkline(sessions, type = "area"))

size is "sm", "md", or "lg"; href turns the whole card into a link.

Lay them out with shad_grid() — min_width fits as many equal columns as will fit, with no breakpoints to maintain:

shad_grid(
  shad_value_box("$48,120", "Revenue", delta = "+12.4%"),
  shad_value_box("1,204", "Sessions", delta = "-3.1%"),
  shad_value_box("2.4%", "Conversion", delta = "0.0%", delta_direction = "neutral"),
  min_width = "12rem"
)

Sparklines and donuts

shad_sparkline() draws "line", "area", "bar", or "step" from a numeric vector, with no axes and no labels. It stretches to fill whatever box it is dropped into — a value box strip, a table cell, an item row:

shad_sparkline(c(31, 40, 28, 51, 42, 62), type = "area")
shad_sparkline(c(-4, -1, 2, 5, -3), type = "bar", color = 2)  # bars hang off zero

Non-finite values break the series rather than being interpolated across, so a gap in the data reads as a gap in the line.

shad_mini_donut() shows a few parts of a whole, with optional content in the middle:

shad_mini_donut(c(62, 24, 14), center = "62%")
shad_mini_donut(c(3, 1), thickness = 1)   # thickness = 1 is a pie

color (and the donut’s colors) take a chart-token index 1–5, or any CSS colour when you need to step outside the palette. Both charts are decorative by default and hidden from screen readers — the number they illustrate is normally right next to them. Pass label when the chart is the only carrier of the information.

The chart card 

shad_chart_container(
  plotOutput("trend", height = "260px"),
  title       = "Revenue by region",
  description = "Last 6 months",
  legend      = TRUE,
  aspect      = "video"   # "video", "square", "wide", or "auto"
)

aspect locks the card’s ratio. Use "auto" when you set an explicit height on the plot yourself — otherwise the two fight and you get letterboxing. plain = TRUE drops the card chrome and keeps only the sizing wrapper, which is what you want when the container already sits inside a shad_card().

legend_labels renders a legend strip in the chart palette, in order, so you can label a plot whose own legend you suppressed:

shad_chart_container(
  plotOutput("stack"),
  title = "Channel mix",
  legend_labels = c("Online", "Retail", "Partner")
)

The palette

shad_chart_colors(n, preset, dark) returns n hex colours from the active theme’s --shad-chart-1 … --shad-chart-6 ramp, interpolating past six:

shad_chart_colors(3)                        # default preset, light
shad_chart_colors(8, "blue", dark = TRUE)   # 8 colours, blue preset, dark mode

shad_tokens(preset, dark) gives you the whole token set as OKLCH strings if you need something the chart ramp doesn’t cover (background, border, muted-foreground, …).

Following the live theme

This is the part that matters. page_shad() themes are switched at runtime — by update_shad_theme() or the user’s dark-mode toggle — and a plot rendered in R has no idea. shad_current_theme() is the bridge: a reactive read of the browser’s current theme that returns list(preset = , dark = ). Touch it inside renderPlot() and the plot re-renders whenever the theme changes.

output$trend <- renderPlot({
  th <- shad_current_theme()          # reactive dependency on the live theme
  ggplot2::ggplot(sales, ggplot2::aes(month, amount, colour = region)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    shad_scale_color_shad(th$preset, th$dark) +
    shad_theme_ggplot2(th$preset, th$dark)
})

Forget shad_current_theme() and your chart keeps its old colours until some unrelated reactive happens to invalidate it.

ggplot2

Helper Does
shad_theme_ggplot2(preset, dark, base_size) A theme() matching the page: background, grid, text, and border colours.
shad_scale_color_shad(preset, dark, ...) Discrete colour scale from the chart ramp.
shad_scale_fill_shad(preset, dark, ...) The same, for fill.

Extra ... pass through to ggplot2::discrete_scale(), so name, labels, and guide work as usual.

ggplot2::ggplot(agg, ggplot2::aes(region, amount, fill = region)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +
  shad_scale_fill_shad(th$preset, th$dark, guide = "none") +
  shad_theme_ggplot2(th$preset, th$dark, base_size = 13) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)

plotly and echarts4r

These take the widget and return it, so they pipe:

output$p <- plotly::renderPlotly({
  th <- shad_current_theme()
  plotly::plot_ly(sales, x = ~month, y = ~amount, color = ~region,
                  type = "scatter", mode = "lines") |>
    shad_theme_plotly(th$preset, th$dark)
})

output$e <- echarts4r::renderEcharts4r({
  th <- shad_current_theme()
  sales |>
    echarts4r::e_charts(month) |>
    echarts4r::e_line(amount) |>
    shad_theme_echarts4r(th$preset, th$dark)
})

Both plotly and echarts4r are Suggests — the helpers error with a clear message if the package isn’t installed.

Base graphics

There is no theme helper, but the palette is just hex, so:

output$bar <- renderPlot({
  th <- shad_current_theme()
  barplot(values, col = shad_chart_colors(length(values), th$preset, th$dark),
          border = NA)
})

Timelines

For event feeds rather than figures:

shad_timeline(
  shad_timeline_item("Order placed", time = "09:12", icon = "check",
                     description = "Payment authorised"),
  shad_timeline_item("Shipped", time = "14:40", status = "active"),
  shad_timeline_item("Delivered", time = "—", status = "muted", last = TRUE),
  align = "left"   # or "alternate"
)
